label: Zyxel GS2220-28
description: Zyxel GS2220-28 - 24x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 plus 4x GbE combo ports (RJ-45 or SFP), L2+ managed NebulaFlex Pro switch, 56 Gbps switching capacity, 42 Mpps, fanless, no PoE.

fabric.note: Zyxel quotes 56 Gbps switching capacity and 42 Mpps forwarding rate for the GS2220-28, with a 1.5 MB packet buffer, 16 K MAC address table, 9 K jumbo frames and 32 MB flash / 256 MB RAM (datasheet Performance table, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf; the product specification table carries the same figures, https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). The switching capacity is the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates - 112 ports at 1G - so it caps nothing the ports cannot already do.

notes: Census from the GS2220 Series datasheet (04/23, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf) and the product specification table (https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). Corrected entry: the previous record listed 24 copper ports plus two separate "sfp1"/"sfp2" cages and carried no source - that is 26 ports for a 28-port box on the wrong hardware, because this model has four combo cages and no dedicated SFP slot (the 2 x SFP slots belong to the 50-port models). The four combo cages are now modelled with both halves (port25/port25-sfp ... port28/port28-sfp): 28 physical ports plus 4 SFP halves. Non-PoE, datasheet PoE cells all "-". Fanless, 0 dBA, 100-240 V AC, 22.5 W with every port loaded, 15.74 W idle - the product specification table prints 15.72 W for the same figure, a 0.02 W disagreement inside Zyxel's own material. Firmware: the series spans two documentation trains. The GS2220-10 User's Guide is Version 4.70 Edition 3 (12/2021, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-10/user_guide/GS2220-10_V4.70_Ed3.pdf) and the GS2220-28HP guide is Version 5.00 Edition 1 (12/2024, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-28HP/user_guide/GS2220-28HP_V5.00_Ed1.pdf). The 4.70 guide calls the RS-232 port "for troubleshooting only" and names the default management address http://192.168.1.1 with admin/1234; the 5.00 guide opens the same port as the CLI door and moves the default management address to https://setup.zyxel (https, not http) with the same admin/1234 or a local credential in cloud mode. The datasheet (04/23) lists features marked "New for V4.80" (new Web interface, Flex link, auto configuration recovery, intuitive cloud connection status), so the datasheet describes a firmware newer than the 4.70 guide and older than the 5.00 one. Console parameters do not change across the two guides: 115200 bps, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control, VT100 emulation, male 9-pin RS-232 cable. The 4.70 guide restricts that port to troubleshooting, while the datasheet feature list offers "Management through Web interface, Console, Telnet, SNMP" and a "Cisco-like CLI" - which is why cli is modelled: telnet, SSH, web and (from firmware 5.00) console all carry it.
